_comment: Written by agent/tools/dashboard.ts. Every figure is derived from the grant's manifest, its allowlist, or the chain — none is typed. The refusal sentences are produced by running the same explainRefusal the payer calls, except the one marked derived:false, which is consensus's answer quoted from a node's actual rejection.

elsewhere.note: The payment settled and the service did not arrive. Why is unknown: the same vendor refuses a payment from an ordinary wallet too, so it is not about this grant, and it has been reported. What the covenant did is the part that is checkable — it bounded what a vendor who takes payment without delivering can take.

timelock.enforcedBy: the covenant, on every spend: claimedDaa >= notBefore. Not a scheduler, not this process, and not revocable by whoever issued the grant.
timelock.termEnforcedBy: the covenant, on every spend: claimedDaa < expiresAt. After it, the grant refuses everything whatever its budget says, and the balance is the principal's to reclaim.

reconciliation.note: This agent keeps no purchase log, so what the covenant says it spent cannot be matched to coins: its payee also receives from other grants, and 21 coins there fit this grant's limits without any being provably its own.

refusals.attempted: pay 0.30000001 KAS to an authorized payee
refusals.refusal: this invoice is 30000001 sompi and the grant's per-payment cap is 30000000. The cap exists to bound what a single decision can do, so it binds here regardless of how much budget remains.

refusals.attempted: pay 5 KAS to an authorized payee
refusals.refusal: this invoice is 500000000 sompi and the grant's per-payment cap is 30000000. The cap exists to bound what a single decision can do, so it binds here regardless of how much budget remains.

refusals.attempted: pay an address the grant never committed to
refusals.refusal: kaspatest:qrxvenxvenxvenxvenxvenxvenxvenxvenxvenxvenxvenxvenxvc3rysjr0d is not on this grant's allowlist, so no inclusion proof places it in the recipients tree. There is no valid transaction that pays them — not one the network would reject, none at all. A grant's payees are fixed at genesis: to pay this vendor you need a grant that committed to them.

kaspatest:pz7fzszt05ggjjkyt8ysmvkewe48x7xfqytq0qxj7hl7wk74kj6vk9uxz45u9 is a pay-to-script-hash address (version 8), and a Warda grant can only pay pay-to-pubkey. The covenant builds the payee output as P2PK(recipient) — there is no transaction shape that pays a script hash from a grant, so this is not something a larger budget or a different grant would fix.

this invoice is 100000001 sompi and only 80000000 remains in the current epoch (3395). The allowance refreshes as the chain advances — and cannot be refreshed by claiming an earlier epoch, which the covenant refuses.

refusals.attempted: pay 0.01 KAS — below what Kaspa will carry
refusals.refusal: this payment of 1000000 sompi is too SMALL to broadcast. Kaspa charges storage mass for the small outputs a transaction creates: this one massed 1000000 against a ceiling of 500000. Nothing about the grant was exceeded and nothing was spent — the amount itself is below what the network will carry.

mission: Monitor the Kaspa network and publish an independent daily digest, unattended. It holds a bounded Warda grant and may buy an approved service when it needs one.

lastRun.note: reading the chain needs no vendor, so this run bought nothing
